quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The new exhibition at the photography museum focuses on street life in the 1960s. Although the pictures are small, they are arranged so cleverly that visitors feel as if they are walking through the city. The museum expects the show to remain open until March. Guided tours are offered every Saturday morning.
quests.question: The way the photos are arranged makes visitors feel like they are in the city.
quests.hint: Read what the small pictures do for visitors.
quests.explanation: The second sentence says the clever arrangement makes people feel they are walking through the city.
quests.evidenceLine: Although the pictures are small, they are arranged so cleverly that visitors feel as if they are walking through the city.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Anyone using the climbing wall for the first time must attend a short safety talk. After that, they can climb without an instructor as long as another adult holds the rope. Children under twelve must always climb with a trainer. The wall is open every day except Monday.
quests.question: New climbers must hear a safety talk before they use the wall.
quests.hint: Look at the rule for first-time users.
quests.explanation: First-time users must attend the talk, so they cannot start climbing before it.
quests.evidenceLine: Anyone using the climbing wall for the first time must attend a short safety talk.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Last year, the town replaced its old street lamps with LED lights. The new lamps use about half as much electricity as the old ones. As a result, the town's electricity bill for lighting fell by nearly forty percent. The mayor called the project a small step toward a greener town.
quests.question: The new street lamps helped lower the town's electricity costs.
quests.hint: Find the result of replacing the lamps.
quests.explanation: The lamps use less electricity, and the passage says the lighting bill fell as a result.
quests.evidenceLine: The new lamps use about half as much electricity as the old ones. As a result, the town's electricity bill for lighting fell by nearly forty percent.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Anil's favorite podcast used to be released every Monday. Since the hosts changed the schedule, a new episode now comes out on Thursdays. He listens to it on his way home from work. The hosts also plan to record a special episode next month.
quests.question: Anil's favorite podcast is still released on Mondays.
quests.hint: Compare the old schedule with the new one.
quests.explanation: The schedule changed, so new episodes now appear on Thursdays.
quests.evidenceLine: Since the hosts changed the schedule, a new episode now comes out on Thursdays.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: When Bao's laptop suddenly shut down, he first checked the power cable, which was plugged in properly. Only after trying a different outlet did he take the laptop to a repair shop. The technician said the battery was faulty.
quests.question: Bao checked the cable before he went to a repair shop.
quests.hint: Put Bao's steps in the order they happened.
quests.explanation: He began with the cable, and the repair shop came only after that.
quests.evidenceLine: When Bao's laptop suddenly shut down, he first checked the power cable, which was plugged in properly. Only after trying a different outlet did he take the laptop to a repair shop.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The local swimming club lowered its monthly fee for children this year. As a result, more than sixty new young swimmers have joined. Parents who register two or more children receive an additional discount.
quests.question: More children joined the club after the fee was lowered.
quests.hint: Look for the result of the lower fee.
quests.explanation: The passage says more than sixty new swimmers joined as a result of the change.
quests.evidenceLine: The local swimming club lowered its monthly fee for children this year. As a result, more than sixty new young swimmers have joined.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Many people think that goldfish have a memory of only three seconds. In fact, experiments have shown that goldfish can remember feeding times and even learn simple tricks. Some have remembered tasks for several months. Researchers now use goldfish to study how fish learn.
quests.question: Goldfish cannot remember anything for longer than a few seconds.
quests.hint: Read what the experiments showed.
quests.explanation: Goldfish remember feeding times and tasks for months, so a few seconds is wrong.
quests.evidenceLine: In fact, experiments have shown that goldfish can remember feeding times and even learn simple tricks. Some have remembered tasks for several months.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city's new tram line connects the airport with the main station. Trams arrive every eight minutes during the day and every fifteen minutes after 10 p.m. A single ticket costs two dollars and is valid for ninety minutes. The line was built in less than two years.
quests.question: Trams run more often at night than during the day.
quests.hint: Compare the gaps between trams at each time.
quests.explanation: Every eight minutes in the day is more frequent than every fifteen at night.
quests.evidenceLine: Trams arrive every eight minutes during the day and every fifteen minutes after 10 p.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Every Sunday evening, Mona spends twenty minutes preparing her schedule for the coming week. On other evenings, she does not plan anything. She says this small habit helps her feel less stressed on Monday mornings.
quests.question: Mona spends twenty minutes on her plans each evening.
quests.hint: How often does Mona sit down to plan?
quests.explanation: She plans on Sunday evenings only, and on other evenings she plans nothing.
quests.evidenceLine: Every Sunday evening, Mona spends twenty minutes preparing her schedule for the coming week. On other evenings, she does not plan anything.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The university library will extend its opening hours during exam week. Instead of closing at 9 p.m., it will stay open until midnight. Students will also be able to borrow laptops for up to four hours at a time. The change applies only until the exams finish.
quests.question: The library will close three hours later than usual during exam week.
quests.hint: Compare the normal and the extended closing times.
quests.explanation: Midnight is three hours after the usual 9 p.m. closing time.
quests.evidenceLine: Instead of closing at 9 p.m., it will stay open until midnight.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Nilufar booked a flight to Istanbul that leaves at 6:10 a.m. Because the airport is far from her home, she has decided to spend the night in a hotel near the terminal. The room costs $70, but the hotel offers a free breakfast. She packed her bag the night before to avoid stress.
quests.question: Nilufar's hotel is far from the airport.
quests.hint: Where is the hotel in relation to the airport?
quests.explanation: The hotel is near the terminal. It is her home that is far away.
quests.evidenceLine: Because the airport is far from her home, she has decided to spend the night in a hotel near the terminal.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Kaito's parents got married in 1995, and his older sister was born two years later. Kaito himself was born in 2003, so there is a gap of several years between the two children. They attend different schools. Their parents say the age difference has never caused problems.
quests.question: Kaito is two years younger than his sister.
quests.hint: Work out the birth years of the two children.
quests.explanation: His sister was born in 1997 and Kaito in 2003, a gap of six years.
quests.evidenceLine: Kaito's parents got married in 1995, and his older sister was born two years later. Kaito himself was born in 2003, so there is a gap of several years between the two children.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In the 1800s, most people in Europe lived in the countryside and worked on farms. As factories appeared in cities, many families moved to find jobs. By 1900, several major cities had grown to more than a million people. Living conditions in many industrial districts were crowded and noisy.
quests.question: Factory jobs encouraged many families to move to cities.
quests.hint: Find why families moved.
quests.explanation: Families moved to cities to find jobs as factories appeared.
quests.evidenceLine: As factories appeared in cities, many families moved to find jobs.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Washing your hands with soap for twenty seconds removes most germs. Using only water is much less effective, because water alone does not break down oils on the skin. Doctors recommend doing this before eating and after using the bathroom. Alcohol-based gels are a useful backup when no sink is nearby.
quests.question: Water alone is a weaker way to clean hands than soap.
quests.hint: Compare soap with plain water.
quests.explanation: The passage calls water alone much less effective than washing with soap.
quests.evidenceLine: Washing your hands with soap for twenty seconds removes most germs. Using only water is much less effective, because water alone does not break down oils on the skin.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Baking bread at home takes patience because the dough must rise for at least an hour. Many beginners open the oven too early, and the loaf falls flat. Experienced bakers wait until the crust is golden brown. Home bakers often keep a small notebook of their recipes.
quests.question: Beginners often spoil their bread by opening the oven too early.
quests.hint: Look for the beginners' common error.
quests.explanation: Opening the oven early makes the loaf fall flat, which spoils it.
quests.evidenceLine: Many beginners open the oven too early, and the loaf falls flat.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Camila lost the first set 6-2 but won the next two sets. Her coach said the change came from a better serve and more patience in long rallies. She now advances to the semifinals. The semifinal will be played on Saturday afternoon.
quests.question: Camila was knocked out of the tournament in this round.
quests.hint: Read the third sentence about what happens next.
quests.explanation: She advances to the semifinals, so she is still in the tournament.
quests.evidenceLine: She now advances to the semifinals.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In Japan, it is common to bow slightly when greeting someone. The deeper the bow, the more respect it shows. Tourists are not expected to bow, but many people appreciate the effort. A quick nod is enough in casual situations.
quests.question: A person who bows lower is showing greater respect.
quests.hint: Read what the depth of a bow tells you.
quests.explanation: The passage links a deeper bow with more respect.
quests.evidenceLine: The deeper the bow, the more respect it shows.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A forecast of sixty percent chance of rain means that rain occurred in about six of ten similar situations. It does not mean that it will rain for sixty percent of the day. Forecasters use this form because a simple yes or no would hide the uncertainty. Many weather apps now show this number for every hour of the day.
quests.question: A sixty percent chance of rain means it will rain for most of the day.
quests.hint: Read the sentence that explains what the number does not mean.
quests.explanation: The passage says the number does not describe how long it will rain.
quests.evidenceLine: It does not mean that it will rain for sixty percent of the day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Male seahorses, not females, carry the babies. The female places her eggs in a pouch on the male's belly, where they stay until they hatch. A single male can give birth to hundreds of tiny seahorses. Their tails can grip seaweed so they do not drift away.
quests.question: Female seahorses carry the eggs until they hatch.
quests.hint: Which parent keeps the eggs?
quests.explanation: The eggs stay in a pouch on the male, not the female.
quests.evidenceLine: Male seahorses, not females, carry the babies. The female places her eggs in a pouch on the male's belly, where they stay until they hatch.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sound cannot travel through empty space because there is no air to carry the vibrations. Astronauts outside a spacecraft therefore talk to each other by radio. Radio waves are a form of light, which can cross a vacuum easily. Their helmets contain small microphones and speakers for this purpose.
quests.question: Astronauts outside a spacecraft can hear each other's voices through the air.
quests.hint: Is there air outside the spacecraft?
quests.explanation: There is no air in space, so astronauts must use radio instead.
quests.evidenceLine: Sound cannot travel through empty space because there is no air to carry the vibrations. Astronauts outside a spacecraft therefore talk to each other by radio.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The word "kindergarten" comes from German and means "children's garden." It was first used in the 1800s by a teacher who believed young children learn best through play. Today the word is used in English and many other languages. Some schools still keep gardens for their youngest pupils.
quests.question: English borrowed the word kindergarten from German.
quests.hint: Look at where the word originally comes from.
quests.explanation: The passage says the word comes from German and is now used in English too.
quests.evidenceLine: The word "kindergarten" comes from German and means "children's garden."

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mr. Alvarez compared two phone plans before choosing one. Plan A costs $25 a month with unlimited data, while Plan B costs $18 a month but includes only five gigabytes. Because he streams videos every day, he chose Plan A. He can cancel the contract after twelve months.
quests.question: Mr. Alvarez chose the cheaper plan.
quests.hint: Compare the prices of the two plans and see which he picked.
quests.explanation: He chose Plan A at $25, and Plan B at $18 was the cheaper one.
quests.evidenceLine: Plan A costs $25 a month with unlimited data, while Plan B costs $18 a month but includes only five gigabytes. Because he streams videos every day, he chose Plan A.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Bamboo is among the fastest growing plants in the world. Some types can grow almost one meter in a single day under the right conditions. Because it regrows quickly after being cut, it is often used as a sustainable building material. Farmers in several countries grow it on land that is unsuitable for other crops.
quests.question: Bamboo is popular as a building material partly because it regrows quickly.
quests.hint: Find the reason bamboo is used for building.
quests.explanation: The third sentence links quick regrowth to its use as a sustainable material.
quests.evidenceLine: Because it regrows quickly after being cut, it is often used as a sustainable building material.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city council wants to reduce traffic downtown. Its plan is to charge drivers a fee to enter the center between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Buses, taxis, and bicycles will not have to pay. The rule will begin next spring after a trial period.
quests.question: Taxis will not be excused from the entry fee.
quests.hint: Read which vehicles are excused from the fee.
quests.explanation: Taxis are named among the vehicles that will not have to pay.
quests.evidenceLine: Buses, taxis, and bicycles will not have to pay.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Recycling one aluminum can saves enough energy to run a television for three hours. Making a new can from raw materials takes far more energy. That is why many countries collect used cans. Collection points are usually placed near supermarkets.
quests.question: Making a new can from raw materials takes less energy than recycling one.
quests.hint: Compare the energy needed for each method.
quests.explanation: New cans made from raw materials take far more energy than recycled ones.
quests.evidenceLine: Recycling one aluminum can saves enough energy to run a television for three hours. Making a new can from raw materials takes far more energy.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Kwesi's landlord promised to repair the heating before winter. The repairs began in October, but a delivery problem delayed the new heater by two weeks. The apartment finally became warm in the middle of November. Kwesi was given a small reduction in rent as an apology.
quests.question: The repairs took longer than planned.
quests.hint: Look for the problem that caused a delay.
quests.explanation: A delivery problem added two weeks, so the work finished later than expected.
quests.evidenceLine: The repairs began in October, but a delivery problem delayed the new heater by two weeks. The apartment finally became warm in the middle of November.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Lifeguards fly a red flag at the beach when the sea is dangerous. A yellow flag means swimmers should be careful, and a green flag means the water is calm. Visitors should check the flag before they enter the water. Lifeguards also check the flags again in the afternoon.
quests.question: A red flag warns people that swimming is risky.
quests.hint: Focus on what the red flag stands for.
quests.explanation: The red flag flies when the sea is dangerous.
quests.evidenceLine: Lifeguards fly a red flag at the beach when the sea is dangerous.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The teachers at Hillside School are testing a new way to give homework. Instead of one long assignment each week, students receive a short task every day. Early results show that students remember the lessons better. Parents received a letter explaining the new system.
quests.question: Hillside School is trying out daily homework tasks in place of one weekly assignment.
quests.hint: Find what is being tested.
quests.explanation: The teachers are testing short daily tasks instead of a long weekly assignment.
quests.evidenceLine: The teachers at Hillside School are testing a new way to give homework. Instead of one long assignment each week, students receive a short task every day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sung-min missed the last train home because the meeting ended late. He had to take a taxi, which cost three times as much as the train ticket. The next morning, he decided to leave meetings earlier. His colleagues promised to help him plan future meetings.
quests.question: The taxi cost less than the train ticket would have.
quests.hint: Compare the taxi fare with the train fare.
quests.explanation: The taxi cost three times the train ticket, so it was more expensive.
quests.evidenceLine: He had to take a taxi, which cost three times as much as the train ticket.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Voice assistants can set alarms, play music, and answer simple questions. They work by recording a short piece of speech and sending it to a server for analysis. Because of this, they need an internet connection for most tasks. Most models also have a button that switches the microphone off.
quests.question: Voice assistants analyze speech without needing an internet connection.
quests.hint: How does the speech get analyzed?
quests.explanation: The speech is sent to a server, so an internet connection is needed for most tasks.
quests.evidenceLine: They work by recording a short piece of speech and sending it to a server for analysis. Because of this, they need an internet connection for most tasks.
